va_eagle_s_gift.blurb: A big, blocky granite slab on the Old Rag side of Shenandoah National Park, holding eleven routes. Most are trad, with a couple of bolted lines mixed in. The grades bunch up around 5.11, with a few easier climbs in the 5.7 to 5.10 range and one 5.12 for the strong. This is classic slab climbing, so expect delicate footwork, and know that protection is better on some lines than on others. The wall sits just past a gap where a giant flake has split away from the main face, a short walk from the neighbouring Whale's Lip wall.

va_haunted_boulder_2.blurb: A bouldering stop in the Guest River Gorge of Southwest Virginia, with eleven problems. It is the first block you meet when you walk down from the upper pull-off into the Upper Jay's section. The boulder is enormous and stands half in the river, with a big roof on one side and a shorter, slabby face next to a deep drop toward the water. Problems range from easy V0 lines to a handful of V2 and V3s, then a few serious outings up to V10, so there is something for most climbers. Water levels shape the landings.

va_postal_crag.blurb: A compact sport wall in the Lower Lightside zone of the Guest River Gorge, Southwest Virginia, with eleven bolted routes. It sits about a minute downstream of the Mammal Wall on the way toward the river. The climbing is short and stout rather than long and sustained. Grades start around 5.9 and run up to the low 5.13s, with the bulk of the routes in the 5.10s and a few 5.12 and 5.13 lines for strong climbers. Moderate routes are scarce, so it suits people already comfortable on 5.10.

va_whale_boulder_the.blurb: A boulder along the Buttermilk Trail in Richmond's James River Park, with eleven problems. It stands right beside the trail, between the paved lot and a small pull-off on Riverside Drive, so there is hardly any walking. The range is wide: a few V0 to V3 warm-ups, a middle group of moderate problems, and several tough lines in the V8 to V11 range for people who want a project.

va_hidden_temple_the.blurb: A small bouldering spot tucked into the woods in the Buttermilks section of Richmond's riverside boulders, with eleven problems. The stone is orange, and the lines are slabby faces leading to a wide ledge under a big roof. The grades are friendly: one very easy warm-up, a few V1 and V2 problems, a solid block of V3 and V4 climbs, and a single V6 as the hardest. It is reached by a short walk of a few minutes from the trailhead parking, using a shortcut off the main trail,.
